note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

chapters.title: Book 1: You control your mind, not the world

episodes.title: It's not the event, it's your story
episodes.hook: Nothing that happened today hurt you. Your story about it did.
episodes.angle: Events are neutral; the damage comes from the judgment we add. Example: two people get the same 'we need to talk' text, one panics, one shrugs.

episodes.title: The traffic jam test
episodes.hook: The traffic jam isn't ruining your morning. You are.
episodes.angle: You cannot move the cars, only your reaction. Example: a driver honking for twenty minutes arrives exactly as late as the one who put on a podcast.

episodes.title: Take away the opinion
episodes.hook: Delete one word from your complaint and the problem shrinks.
episodes.angle: Remove the label 'I've been wronged' and the harm loses its grip. Example: rewriting 'my boss disrespected me' as 'my boss sent a short email'.

episodes.title: The fortress inside
episodes.hook: There's one room nobody can enter without your permission.
episodes.angle: Your inner judgment is a citadel; insults and bad luck stay outside unless you let them in. Example: a referee booed by a full stadium who still calls the game calmly.

episodes.title: Is it in your control?
episodes.hook: Before you worry, ask one question.
episodes.angle: Sort every worry into 'mine to act on' or 'not mine'. Example: a student who stops refreshing the grades page and starts the next assignment.

episodes.title: Expect difficult people
episodes.hook: You'll meet someone annoying today. Good. Now you're ready.
episodes.angle: Expecting rudeness in the morning removes the shock later. Example: a barista who mentally prepares for the grumpy regular and ends up laughing at him.

episodes.title: They don't know better
episodes.hook: The person who wronged you thinks they're right.
episodes.angle: People act on what seems good to them; anger at ignorance is wasted. Example: the coworker who steals your idea genuinely believes he improved it.

episodes.title: The best revenge
episodes.hook: The best revenge is not becoming like them.
episodes.angle: Copying someone's cruelty lets them win twice. Example: refusing to answer a nasty group-chat message with an even nastier one.

episodes.title: Stop needing their applause
episodes.hook: Imagine doing your best work and nobody ever finds out.
episodes.angle: Praise adds nothing to a good act, like an emerald doesn't need compliments. Example: a nurse on a night shift nobody will ever thank.

episodes.title: Memento mori
episodes.hook: You could leave life right now. Let that decide what you do next.
episodes.angle: Remembering death is not dark, it cuts out the trivial. Example: someone who stops arguing in comment sections after a health scare.

episodes.title: Everyone forgets everyone
episodes.hook: In a hundred years, nobody will remember your embarrassing moment.
episodes.angle: Fame and shame both fade fast, so neither is worth your peace. Example: try naming a famous person from 1820.

episodes.title: The present is all you have
episodes.hook: You can only lose this moment. Not your past, not your future.
episodes.angle: Nobody can lose a life they don't have yet; only the present is real. Example: a gamer who stops grinding for the 'someday' save file and plays the level in front of him.

episodes.title: Change is the rule
episodes.hook: Everything you love is already changing. That's not bad news.
episodes.angle: The river is never the same; resisting change causes the suffering. Example: a band whose fans hate the new album, then call it a classic ten years later.

chapters.title: Book 4: Getting out of bed and doing the work

episodes.title: Why get out of bed?
episodes.hook: You weren't born to lie under a warm blanket.
episodes.angle: A tree, a bee and an ant all do their job; your job is to be human. Example: snoozing the alarm for the fifth time and the argument that finally gets you up.

episodes.title: Do the next right thing
episodes.hook: Stop planning the perfect life. Do the next right thing.
episodes.angle: Focus on the single act in front of you, done well, like it's your last. Example: a messy room cleaned one drawer at a time.

episodes.title: The obstacle is the way
episodes.hook: What stands in your way becomes the way.
episodes.angle: An obstacle can be turned into training for the exact virtue you need. Example: a canceled flight turned into the day you finally finish the book.

episodes.title: Talk less about being good
episodes.hook: Stop arguing about what a good person is. Be one.
episodes.angle: Debate is cheap; action is the proof. Example: someone posting long threads about kindness while ignoring a friend's text.
